_notes: Non-rendered field: destination facts and seasonality findings only. The app ignores keys it does not know. Planning rationale and open questions are kept outside the repo.
TRIP LENGTH: scoped at 17 days because international access to Korea currently requires a connection. The flight-access reasoning behind that number is in the private planning notes.

SEASONALITY — FOLIAGE (re-verified 30 Aug 2026): the 2026 forecast has firmed up and is EARLIER than the long-term normal. First colour on Seoraksan's upper slopes around 27-30 September; peak across the whole mountain forecast for 12-15 OCTOBER 2026. For comparison the long-term normal peak is ~17 Oct, and it ran late in recent years (24 Oct 2025, 29 Oct 2024). The Korea Meteorological Administration publishes its official map in early September — check it before fixing dates. A 12-15 October peak sits much closer to the usual travel window than earlier estimates suggested.
SEASONALITY — OTHERWISE: no closure risk anywhere. Korean national parks, temples, markets and transport all run year-round, and October is dry, mild and the single best month to visit.

LOGISTICS: no car for the Seoul days — the metro is better and parking is awful. Pick the car up on day 6 and drop it in Busan. Driving in Korea requires an International Driving Permit alongside a national licence; roads and signage are excellent and tolls are automatic.
LOGISTICS: the return runs Busan to Seoul by KTX (about 2h40) rather than driving back, so the last day is not spent on the motorway.

CARD CAPTIONS — PRIMARY (migrated 2026-08-30): Seoul: Four nights at the start, and no car until you leave. | Seoraksan National Park: 2026 peak forecast for 12–15 October; upper slopes turn from late September. | Busan & Gamcheon: Two nights at the end, before the train back.

CARD CAPTIONS — NATURE (migrated 2026-08-30): Ulsanbawi Ridge: About 8 km return, with 800-plus steps at the top. | Biseondae & Sinheungsa: About 5 km and level throughout — the gentle Seoraksan option. | Dodamsambong, Danyang: Lit after dark; the riverside path is a ten-minute stroll. | Sobaeksan National Park: The same forest as Seoraksan, without the crowds or the staircases. | The East Coast Drive: Highway 7 runs the coast for 200 km with very little traffic.

CARD CAPTIONS — CITIES (migrated 2026-08-30): Seoul: Four nights at the start, and no car until you leave. | Sokcho: Twenty minutes from the Seoraksan park gate. | Gyeongju: The mounds are lit after dark and free to walk among. | Busan: Three hours from Seoul by KTX if you drop the car early. | Jeonju: Stay inside the old quarter if you can — it empties after dark. | Danyang: The riverside promenade is lit at night and lined with food stalls.

CARD CAPTIONS — FOOD (migrated 2026-08-30): Korean Fried Chicken: Order banban and you get half plain, half sauced. | Samgyeopsal: Priced per portion with a two-portion minimum; staff do the grilling. | Tteokbokki & Street Snacks: Sindang-dong in Seoul is the street that specialises in it. | Jeonju Bibimbap: Gajok Hoegwan and Hankookjib are the two long-standing institutions. | Kimchi: There are over a hundred regional kinds; every restaurant has its own. | Hotteok & Bingsu: Hotteok carts appear on the street as soon as it turns cold.

CARD CAPTIONS — THINGS TO DO (migrated 2026-08-30): A Day at the DMZ: Licensed tours only — no independent access. Closed Mondays; bring passports. | Namsan & the Hilltop Gym: Cable car from Myeongdong, or 40 minutes up on foot through the park. | Seoul Sky: Go about an hour before sunset to get the city in both lights. | The Han River by Bike: Ttukseom and Yeouido have the biggest rental points; best after dark. | Gwangjang Market: Busiest early evening; bring cash and point at what looks good.
destination: South Korea — Seoul, Seoraksan & the South
title: Markets, Mountains & Fried Chicken: A South Korea Road Trip

heroImage.caption: Autumn colour in Seoraksan National Park

brief: The food trip, with mountains attached. Seoul first — markets, street food, neon, hanok lanes and some of the best casual eating anywhere — then a car east to Seoraksan for granite peaks and autumn colour, down through river country and old Gyeongju, and a finish in Busan among painted hillside houses. Safe, hyper-modern, and cheap once you land.

facts.bestSeason: Mid–late October — dry and mild, and the only window that catches Seoraksan's colour
facts.language: Korean; English signage is good, spoken English is patchy outside Seoul
facts.driving: Right-hand traffic, excellent roads; International Driving Permit required
facts.flightsWithinTrip: None — the whole route is covered by car and one KTX train

primary.heading: Eat first, hike later
primary.intro: Four nights in Seoul to get properly through the markets, then a car east into granite mountains, south through river country to the town that invented the food, and a finish on the coast.

nature.heading: Granite, forest and river bends
nature.intro: Korea is seventy percent mountain. Seoraksan is the dramatic end of it — spires, staircases and the country's earliest autumn colour — while Danyang and Sobaeksan are gentler, greener and nearly empty.

cities.heading: Neon, hanok and painted hillsides
cities.intro: Seoul stacks glass towers over wooden courtyard houses. Gyeongju is low-rise and a thousand years old. Busan climbs a hillside in pastel.

food.heading: The reason to come
food.intro: Pork grilled at the table, fried chicken at midnight, rice cakes from a cart, and market stalls that each do one dish perfectly. Cheap, everywhere, and open late.

why.heading: What Korea gives you that Europe can't
why.intro: A completely different register — hyper-modern, exceptionally safe, and organised from top to bottom around eating at all hours.

thingsToDo.heading: Border tours, bathhouses and a tower
thingsToDo.intro: Seoul rewards just walking out of the door, but a few things are worth planning around — the border in particular, which is the one thing here you cannot organise yourself.

itinerary.description: Land, sleep at an airport hotel, and let the time difference settle before starting.
Four nights and no car — palaces and hanok lanes, market food every night, a hilltop park, and a day up to the DMZ.
Pick up the car and drive east. Granite spires, temple forest, a cable car, and the country's earliest autumn colour.
River bends and limestone peaks, caves, a lakeside town famous for garlic bread, and quiet mountain trails.
Grass burial mounds in the middle of town, hillside temples, and a street of food stalls that runs late.
Painted houses stacked up a hillside at Gamcheon, huge markets, and a temple built onto the sea cliffs.
Korea's food capital — 700 restored hanok houses, and the dish this country is best known for, made where it was invented.
Drop the car, KTX back to Seoul in under three hours, and fly home.

primaryHighlights.title: Seoul
primaryHighlights.description: The main reason to come. Markets, night-time street food, hanok lanes and glass towers stacked on top of each other.
primaryHighlights.caption: Hanok alley at blue hour

primaryHighlights.title: Seoraksan National Park
primaryHighlights.description: Granite spires over dense forest, and the first place in Korea to turn colour every autumn.
primaryHighlights.caption: Granite peaks above pine forest

primaryHighlights.title: Busan & Gamcheon
primaryHighlights.description: A hillside of pastel houses above the sea, murals everywhere, and the biggest street-food markets in the country.
primaryHighlights.caption: Gamcheon's pastel hillside houses

natureHighlights.title: Ulsanbawi Ridge
natureHighlights.description: Seoraksan's signature hike — around 8 km return to a granite crest, with a long staircase at the end. Big commitment, bigger view.
natureHighlights.caption: Jagged granite ridge with pines

natureHighlights.title: Biseondae & Sinheungsa
natureHighlights.description: A valley walk past a giant bronze Buddha to a gorge full of smooth granite slabs.
natureHighlights.caption: Granite summit ridge, Seoraksan

natureHighlights.title: Dodamsambong, Danyang
natureHighlights.description: Three rock pinnacles standing in the Namhan river — the calm, green, water-and-mountain half of the trip.
natureHighlights.caption: Dodamsambong's three river pinnacles

natureHighlights.title: Sobaeksan National Park
natureHighlights.description: Rolling forested ridges with well-graded trails and hardly anyone else on them.
natureHighlights.caption: Autumn colour on a forested ridge

natureHighlights.title: The East Coast Drive
natureHighlights.description: Pine forest on one side, open water on the other, for as long as you feel like driving.
natureHighlights.caption: Pine forest path by the sea

cityHighlights.title: Seoul
cityHighlights.description: Ten million people, mountains on three sides, and a skyline you can see whole from a hilltop park in the middle of it.
cityHighlights.caption: Seoul skyline at sunset

cityHighlights.title: Sokcho
cityHighlights.description: A low-key harbour town with a beach and the mountains filling the western horizon.
cityHighlights.caption: Fishing boat at Daepo Port

cityHighlights.title: Gyeongju
cityHighlights.description: A thousand-year-old capital that is now a low-rise town scattered with grass burial mounds.
cityHighlights.caption: Gyeongju's grass burial mounds

cityHighlights.title: Busan
cityHighlights.description: A port city built up the sides of steep hills, with a pastel-painted village on one of them and a temple on the sea cliffs.
cityHighlights.caption: Haeundae high-rises across the water

cityHighlights.title: Jeonju
cityHighlights.description: Seven hundred restored wooden hanok houses in one quarter, and a food culture the rest of the country defers to.
cityHighlights.caption: Hanok rooftops over Jeonju

cityHighlights.title: Danyang
cityHighlights.description: A small town wrapped around a bend in the Namhan river, with limestone peaks straight behind it.
cityHighlights.caption: River rocks below misty hills

culinaryHighlights.title: Korean Fried Chicken
culinaryHighlights.description: Twice-fried, glazed or plain, ordered late at night and eaten straight out of the box. Reason enough for the flight.
culinaryHighlights.caption: A plate of fried chicken

culinaryHighlights.title: Samgyeopsal
culinaryHighlights.description: Thick pork belly grilled at the table, wrapped in lettuce with garlic and sauce. The default Korean dinner, and a great one.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Pork belly grilling with garlic

culinaryHighlights.title: Tteokbokki & Street Snacks
culinaryHighlights.description: Chewy rice cakes in chilli sauce, fried skewers, egg bread and hotteok — the whole street-cart repertoire, everywhere, cheap.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Rice cakes in chilli sauce

culinaryHighlights.title: Jeonju Bibimbap
culinaryHighlights.description: The dish in the town that invented it — brass bowl, raw beef, thirty toppings, and a queue of Koreans who have driven here for it.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Chefs mixing bibimbap at a festival

culinaryHighlights.title: Kimchi
culinaryHighlights.description: Fermented cabbage with chilli and garlic, served free with absolutely every meal, and made in vast earthenware jars that sit outside houses.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Rows of earthenware kimchi jars

culinaryHighlights.title: Hotteok & Bingsu
culinaryHighlights.description: Sweet syrup-filled pancakes fried on a griddle in winter, and mountains of shaved milk ice under fruit or red bean the rest of the year.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Hotteok frying on a griddle

thingsToDo.title: A Day at the DMZ
thingsToDo.description: The Third Infiltration Tunnel, the Dora Observatory looking straight into North Korea, and the bridge where prisoners were exchanged.
thingsToDo.caption: View over the DMZ

thingsToDo.title: Namsan & the Hilltop Gym
thingsToDo.description: Walk or ride up Seoul's central mountain for the whole skyline, past one of the free open-air gyms that sit at the top of most Korean parks.
thingsToDo.caption: Namsan tower at sunset

thingsToDo.title: Seoul Sky
thingsToDo.description: The observation deck on floors 117 to 123 of the Lotte World Tower, with a glass floor and the city laid out flat below.
thingsToDo.caption: Purple sunset over Seoul's skyline

thingsToDo.title: The Han River by Bike
thingsToDo.description: Hire a bike at any riverside park and ride a flat, continuous path right through the middle of the city, with convenience stores the whole way.
thingsToDo.caption: Bikes by the river at night

thingsToDo.title: Gwangjang Market
thingsToDo.description: A covered market where hundreds of stalls each cook one dish in front of you — mung-bean pancakes, knife-cut noodles, rice rolls — eaten on plastic stools.
thingsToDo.caption: Crowded market alley, flags overhead

otherPerks: Food is served until 2am, and a proper meal runs about eight euros
Jjimjilbang — 24-hour bathhouses with hot pools, saunas and sleeping rooms, for about ten euros
Seoraksan's colour is forecast to peak 12–15 October this year
Convenience stores are genuinely good — hot food, seating, open around the clock
One of the safest countries anywhere; nothing feels off, at any hour
More cafés per person than anywhere on earth, and the coffee is taken seriously
Underground malls, market halls and whole streets of hardware shops
KTX trains at 300 km/h, so dropping the car never strands you
